Since you're looking at Bootstrap here and there like you said, take a look at the LESS version. https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/tree/master/less

They have by far the best implementation of LESS I have seen to date.

It's overwhelming at first, but the main files are bootstrap.less, variables.less, and mixins.less.

Take a look at variables.less and it should get you excited. You define your colors, font styles, margins, padding, etc there and use them else where. So if you want to make a change, one file one place and it changes in all the other files when you compile it to CSS.

I could talk about it forever cause it really is a life changer.

As for as C# and ASP.NET I don't have any experience with. Scala, Java, and Ruby are my background. But I am 110% sure there are tools out there for using and deploying LESS on .NET projects.

The keyword you would search for is "asset pipeline". So when researching, I would look for ".NET asset pipeline" or similar search terms. An asset pipeline handles auto-compile for your development environment so you can make changes and just refresh the web page to see those changes like you normally would using CSS.

When you deploy the project, the asset pipeline should handle the one time compile to make it permanently CSS in your production website which you obviously don't want compiling the LESS on every page refresh.

Most asset pipelines are smart enough these days to detect file changes and only compile when it detects a file change. At least in the frameworks I use.

Additionally, if you find an asset pipeline that creates source maps for you, you can actually see the LESS in your browser and edit the LESS in the browser! Both Chrome and Firefox support source maps.
